_comment: COMPILED from docs/rubric/01_*.md...10_*.md + 11_WEIGHTS_THRESHOLDS_CONFIG.md — do not hand-edit. Run npm run compile:rubric.

remediation.quick_win: document the gap, create the upgrade ticket with a date.
remediation.structural: parallel runtime upgrade plan — run new runtime in CI behind a feature gate, migrate one service at a time, dual-run in prod. For truly stuck runtimes, isolate behind a facade and treat like a rewrite candidate.
remediation.gold_standard: Every production runtime within its vendor-supported window; CI builds a canary job on the current runtime; a deprecation calendar exists and is reviewed quarterly.

remediation.quick_win: enable Dependabot/Renovate with major-update grouping and a monthly budget.
remediation.structural: "upgrade train" — pick one major hop per quarter, keep intermediate commits shippable, use the dependency graph from tools to sequence hops (don't skip majors). Establish a "never more than 1 major behind" policy for core deps.
remediation.gold_standard: Core framework within 1 major of current; < 30% of direct deps behind by a major; automatic update PRs flowing weekly; majors scheduled explicitly on the roadmap.

remediation.quick_win: audit the dependency surface for abandoned libs and create a removal/swap ticket with a date.
remediation.structural: replace load-bearing abandoned libs with maintained alternatives or fork-and-own with a maintenance budget; pin to the exact version and wrap it behind your own interface so it's swappable.
remediation.gold_standard: Every load-bearing dependency either actively maintained or deliberately forked-and-owned; a quarterly "library health" review is on the calendar; no archived repos in the dependency surface.

remediation.quick_win: turn deprecation warnings into a CI-visible report (not silent); fix the 20 highest-value warnings.
remediation.structural: treat deprecation debt like feature debt — a quarterly "modernize the deprecated surface" slice; keep the target version's removal list as a tracked checklist.
remediation.gold_standard: Zero deprecation warnings in the core module build; a CI gate that fails (or reports) on new deprecation warnings; removal timelines tracked.

remediation.quick_win: generate an SBOM (`syft . > sbom.json`), wire it into CI, publish attribution files.
remediation.structural: add a license gate to CI (fail on GPL in closed-source), replace copyleft deps, retire unknown-license packages, review vendored code for stripped notices.
remediation.gold_standard: SBOM generated and attested on every release; license policy enforced in CI; zero unknown licenses; copyleft list reviewed quarterly and signed off.

remediation.quick_win: run `knip`/`depcheck`, remove unused direct deps, enable `npm dedupe`/lockfile optimization in CI.
remediation.structural: set a budget (e.g., "no net-new transitive deps without review"), replace kitchen-sink libs with narrow ones, dedupe semver ranges, and periodically prune.
remediation.gold_standard: Transitive count within a declared budget; zero unused direct deps; single version of every critical lib; dependency review is part of code review.

remediation.quick_win: commit the lockfile, switch CI to `npm ci`/`pip install --require-hashes`/`--frozen-lockfile`, add a "lockfile up-to-date" CI check.
remediation.structural: adopt content-hash pinning, build from clean containers, produce provenance attestations (SLSA level 1→2), verify registry integrity.
remediation.gold_standard: Lockfile committed and current; CI immutable install; two clean builds produce byte-identical artifacts; SLSA provenance generated per release.

remediation.quick_win: quantify the coupling (which modules touch framework-specific APIs directly) and freeze scope on framework-dependent features.
remediation.structural: extract the framework behind a facade at the boundaries (ports & adapters), migrate incrementally module-by-module on the critical path, keep the system runnable through the whole migration.
remediation.gold_standard: Framework either current-and-supported, or the core logic is framework-independent behind an interface with an active migration plan.

remediation.quick_win: inventory the skew, pick a "platform baseline" version, and make new work use it.
remediation.structural: establish a platform/boilerplate team with a version cadence; migrate oldest-first on the critical path; add cross-service tests for the shared contract; sunset divergent majors with deadlines.
remediation.gold_standard: One supported major of every core dependency per system; upgrade cadence managed centrally; a new service starts on the platform baseline.

remediation.quick_win: run socket.dev/scorecard immediately, pin all CI actions to SHAs, enable `--lockfile` integrity and verified-publisher checks, scan for squat-named packages.
remediation.structural: registry pinning, SBOM + provenance attestation (SLSA), private registry mirror with scanning, incident runbook for a compromised package, least-privilege CI tokens.
remediation.gold_standard: Scorecard ≥ 8, all actions SHA-pinned, provenance verified per release, malware scan wired into CI as a gate, squatted-name watchlist.

remediation.quick_win: carve the top 5 offenders by automated extract-method (IDE-assisted, with tests), add a complexity budget to CI (`eslint max-complexity`, SonarQube gate).
remediation.structural: a structured decomposition of God Classes by responsibility; strangle complexity behind facades; pair the two riskiest files on a refactor sprint.
remediation.gold_standard: Complexity budget enforced in CI; max method complexity < 15; no file > 1,000 LOC; the top-decile complexity list is shrinking and tracked.

remediation.quick_win: draw the DSM, pick the 3 highest-fan-in hubs, wrap them behind interfaces and shrink their API.
remediation.structural: define bounded contexts and enforce them with ArchUnit-style rules in CI; extract the shared hub into a stable, narrow contract; invert dependencies toward stable abstractions.
remediation.gold_standard: Acyclic dependency graph at the module boundary; every module has narrow, explicit dependencies; teams can change their module without coordination (tested via a chaos week).

remediation.quick_win: add an arch test (ArchUnit/import-linter) and fix the top violations; enforce at PR time.
remediation.structural: rebuild the lost layers — extract domain into its own module, move persistence behind repositories, keep UI thin; do it one vertical slice at a time.
remediation.gold_standard: Architecture rules enforced in CI; a 30-minute vertical-slice tour confirms correct directions; business rules live in the domain layer only.

remediation.quick_win: run knip/vulture, delete safely (git history preserves), remove orphaned endpoints and the routes that point to them.
remediation.structural: a "no dead code" PR gate (knip in CI, fail on new unreferenced exports), flag retirement policy (flags > 6 months get removed or justified), quarterly pruning ritual.
remediation.gold_standard: Dead-code scan clean in CI; every feature flag has an owner and a retirement date; all prod endpoints are in an API inventory with traffic.

indicators.name: Code Churn vs. Defect Hot Spots

remediation.quick_win: put the top hot spot behind a designated owner, add targeted tests, freeze feature scope on it for one sprint.
remediation.structural: redesign the hot spot — decompose by responsibility, rewrite the risky core with tests first, rotate engineers to avoid bus-factor in the fix. Track the metric quarterly to prove improvement.
remediation.gold_standard: Churn evenly distributed relative to responsibility; no file in the top churn∩defect intersection for two quarters; hot-spot list tracked in the refactoring backlog.

remediation.quick_win: introduce interface seams around the 3 worst-coupled cores, add a couple of tests to prove the seams work.
remediation.structural: adopt the modern architecture incrementally — introduce a DI container, extract modules with enforced boundaries, wrap legacy access behind ports, migrate vertical slices one at a time.
remediation.gold_standard: Core logic testable without live infrastructure; DI and module boundaries standard; new features land in the modern style while legacy shrinks.

remediation.quick_win: inject the clock/random/IO at the seams you can reach; make the top 5 singletons instances with explicit wiring.
remediation.structural: eliminate globals by constructor injection; make state explicit and owned; introduce a proper initialization/DI lifecycle; enforce "no static mutable" with a lint.
remediation.gold_standard: All dependencies explicit and injected; time/random/IO behind interfaces; test suite passes under random/parallel execution; zero mutable statics in core.

remediation.quick_win: run jscpd, consolidate the top clusters behind a shared library (start with the business-critical ones).
remediation.structural: establish a shared internal library with a review process; kill duplicates at PR time (clone scan in CI); migrate duplicated logic incrementally with tests preserving behavior.
remediation.gold_standard: Duplication < 10%; core business rules exist exactly once, in one owned library; clone scan in CI fails new duplication.

remediation.quick_win: ship a repo-map/context file, co-locate tests for the top core modules, define a task runner of record with a fresh-clone CI proof.
remediation.structural: seam extraction on core (ports), docs-as-code freshness (DOCS-09), a recurring "agent completes task X from fresh clone" acceptance test as a quality gate.
remediation.gold_standard: From a fresh clone, an agent (or new hire) can locate the module, run its tests, and land a scoped change within one session; navigation aids match disk; core is testable without live infra.

remediation.quick_win: move the top flags to an externalized flag source with owners + retirement dates, externalize prod config into a per-env injected pipeline.
remediation.structural: config-as-code injected per environment, a flag lifecycle policy (owner, TTL, removal ceremony), a rule that prod values never live in the repo.
remediation.gold_standard: Zero hardcoded toggles in core; every flag owned with a retirement date; config injected per env from one source; rollback = flag flip, not code change.

remediation.quick_win: enable `strict`/`strictNullChecks` on the smallest core module, fix the fallout, expand module by module; add `mypy --strict` to CI incrementally with a ban-list.
remediation.structural: adopt explicit null-safety (Option/Result types), eliminate `any` with real types at boundaries, add type coverage gate (e.g., `typescript coverage > X%`).
remediation.gold_standard: Strict mode on across the system; typed coverage > 90%; null/type errors < 2% of incidents; boundary types (API, DB, events) fully defined.

indicators.name: Duplicated Cross-Cutting Concerns (auth, logging, error handling, transactions)

remediation.quick_win: audit for missing shared middleware and missed auth sites; move the top repeated concern (auth) to framework middleware.
remediation.structural: centralize each concern (authN/authZ, logging, error mapping, validation, transactions) into one owned infrastructure layer with tests; wire via framework interceptors; add security tests that assert every endpoint enforces auth.
remediation.gold_standard: Every cross-cutting concern implemented once, in infrastructure, enforced by framework; a security test walks all routes asserting auth coverage; zero manual auth in controllers.

remediation.quick_win: add a real coverage gate (fail below threshold) on core modules only, and instrument the trend.
remediation.structural: invest in testing the highest-churn/highest-risk modules first (correlate with ARCH-05), write tests as part of every bug fix (see coverage climb), make coverage a tracked product metric.
remediation.gold_standard: Branch coverage > 80% on core modules; coverage gate enforced in CI; coverage trend visible on a dashboard and rising or stable.

remediation.quick_win: quarantine flaky tests (run separately, don't block but do report), fix the top 5 by root cause (sleeps → waits, shared DB → test DBs, order-dependence → isolation).
remediation.structural: make tests hermetic (see TEST-07), add flake detection to CI (auto-quarantine + report), hold the line: no new flaky tests.
remediation.gold_standard: Flake rate < 2%; zero "rerun to pass" culture; flaky tests auto-quarantined and tracked to fix within a sprint.

remediation.quick_win: move the top 20 E2E tests' logic down to integration/unit level (test the service, not the click).
remediation.structural: rebuild the pyramid over time — write unit tests for all domain logic, integration for boundaries, keep E2E for < 10 user journeys; budget E2E runtime.
remediation.gold_standard: Classic pyramid (e.g., 70/20/10); E2E < 10% runtime; failures localize within seconds; E2E covers only true user journeys.

remediation.quick_win: parallelize across shards/workers, move slow E2E out of the merge gate (nightly), fix the slowest 10 tests.
remediation.structural: attack root causes — pyramid rebalance (TEST-03), hermetic fast tests, caching, and a runtime budget with a gate.
remediation.gold_standard: Suite < 10 min P95; every engineer runs the suite before merge; a runtime budget enforced in CI.

remediation.quick_win: re-enable or delete each skip deliberately (delete-with-justification or fix-with-test); no skips without a linked ticket and owner.
remediation.structural: CI gate that fails on new skips without a ticket; a monthly "skip inventory" review; fix the top skipped module's root cause.
remediation.gold_standard: < 2% skipped, all with tickets + owners, none older than a sprint; new skips auto-blocked.

remediation.quick_win: characterisation-test the core (capture current behavior, lock it), then fix the top 3 divergent behaviors.
remediation.structural: treat the core as the highest test priority — require tests on every core change, build a test-heavy "crown jewels" suite, tie core coverage to the gate.
remediation.gold_standard: All 10 core journeys have tests; core module coverage > 80%; a core change without tests cannot merge; incidents on core paths are rare and never "first discovery."

remediation.quick_win: run randomized + parallel CI to surface the worst offenders, fix shared-fixture tests, replace sleeps with waits.
remediation.structural: hermetic test infrastructure — per-test DBs (Testcontainers), fixtures scoped to each test, deterministic time, no network in unit tests, parallel by default.
remediation.gold_standard: Suite passes under random order and full parallelism on a fresh container; zero sleeps; tests never touch shared live infrastructure.

remediation.quick_win: add lint + SAST (Semgrep/CodeQL/SonarQube) as failing stages, add a coverage gate on core, block admin bypass (require justification audit).
remediation.structural: define the quality bar in code (lint rules, complexity budgets, coverage thresholds, security checks) and let CI enforce it; tie all gates to the same config the team reviews.
remediation.gold_standard: CI fails on lint, SAST, coverage, complexity, and security findings; bypasses are impossible or audited; the gates' config is itself reviewed.

remediation.quick_win: run mutation on the top-criticality module, fix the highest-value survivors (add assertions, kill branches).
remediation.structural: run mutation on core modules in CI (time-boxed), use surviving-mutant count as a tracked quality metric, strengthen weak assertions.
remediation.gold_standard: Core module mutation score ≥ 85%; mutation runs in CI on the core; survivors are reviewed and justified.

remediation.quick_win: break the coupling — assert behavior not internals (mock at boundaries, not implementation), stabilize flaky snapshots, stop auto-updating snapshots.
remediation.structural: treat the suite as a product (owner, budget, KPIs), refactor tests to test contracts not internals, track test-maintenance share as a metric with a ceiling.
remediation.gold_standard: < 10% of commits are test maintenance; tests break only when behavior changes; the suite is seen as an asset, not a tax.

remediation.quick_win: patch the open Criticals/Highs in the exposure window — today; re-scan.
remediation.structural: a patch SLA policy (Critical ≤ 7 days, High ≤ 30), automated patching (Dependabot/Renovate auto-merge with CI as the gate), and a "no open Critical in prod" rule enforced by the security review.
remediation.gold_standard: Zero open Criticals; Highs < 30 days; automated scans in CI; patch SLA documented and met for 4 straight quarters.

remediation.quick_win: rotate EVERY leaked credential immediately (the exposure window starts at commit time, not discovery time), remove from current tree, switch to env vars.
remediation.structural: adopt a secret manager + injection (Vault, Secrets Manager), ban secrets in code via CI scanners on every commit *and* a history scrub, least-privilege per environment, kill the "secrets in docs" habit.
remediation.gold_standard: Zero secrets in the tree or history; secrets injected at runtime from a manager; CI blocks secret commits; rotation drill run annually.

remediation.quick_win: enable modern headers (HSTS/CSP via middleware), upgrade TLS, fix the top reachable injection points with parameterized queries and validation.
remediation.structural: framework defaults (most modern frameworks secure headers by default — upgrade), SAST+DAST in CI, input validation at every entry, an injection-class bug ban (semantic gate).
remediation.gold_standard: A+ header/TLS grades, zero reachable Top-10 findings, SAST+DAST wired into CI, validation at all boundaries.

remediation.quick_win: kill default creds, add auth + server-side authorization to every endpoint (route registry), enable MFA on privileged roles, fix the top IDORs.
remediation.structural: move to managed identity (SSO/OIDC, platform IAM), policy-based authorization (OPA/AWS IAM/ABAC), automated authz tests (walk every route asserting enforcement), session best practices.
remediation.gold_standard: All endpoints server-side auth'd and authz'd, MFA everywhere privileged, managed SSO + policy engine, authz coverage test in CI.

remediation.quick_win: add audit logging to the top admin/PII/auth paths with a structured schema, ship logs to an external durable sink, set retention.
remediation.structural: treat audit as a compliance requirement — append-only/crypto-chained where needed, centralized log platform, automated test asserting every sensitive action produces an audit event.
remediation.gold_standard: Every admin/PII/auth event logged structured (actor, action, target, time, request ID), durable, retained per policy, and tamper-evident; an automated coverage test exists.

remediation.quick_win: use tooling to map reachable chains to top-level packages, plan removals/forks of the top offenders, add deep scanning to CI.
remediation.structural: prune the graph (replace deep-chain producers), vendoring review, dependency budget (ECOS-06), provenance verification, and an incident runbook for "malicious package found."
remediation.gold_standard: Deep scanning in CI with reachability intelligence; zero malware; vulnerable chains mapped and justified; unmaintained chains trending to zero.

remediation.quick_win: enable Dependabot/Renovate with auto-merge on green for patch/minor updates, act on the security-only PRs first.
remediation.structural: a scheduled patch lane (weekly security window, CI gates), environment-per-ticket to stage patches, measured SLA with an executive dashboard.
remediation.gold_standard: Patches automated, applied within SLA (Crit ≤ 7d, High ≤ 30d), CI validates every patch, zero manual patch heroics.

remediation.quick_win: map the top 10 required controls to evidence today, automate the biggest evidence gaps (logs, backups, review reports).
remediation.structural: continuous compliance automation (CSPM tools, evidence pipelines), close the accepted-risk list to a bounded, tracked set, encryption at rest everywhere, retention/erasure as engineering backlog items.
remediation.gold_standard: Controls auto-evidenced, near-zero accepted-risk, encryption + retention/erasure automated, audit-ready at any moment.

remediation.quick_win: stand up fuzz harnesses for the top 3 untrusted parsers, run sanitizer builds, harden validation at those boundaries (limits, types, structure).
remediation.structural: fuzz-in-CI for parser-adjacent code, migrate memory-unsafe parsers, input-validation as a platform concern, adversarial corpus maintenance.
remediation.gold_standard: Every untrusted parser fuzzed in CI with sanitizers, zero standing crashes, validation layers reject early and clearly.

remediation.quick_win: add Semgrep/CodeQL failing gates, secret scan on history + CI, TRIVY on images — this week.
remediation.structural: a security-as-quality pipeline (SAST, deps, secrets, container, DAST on staging, threat modelling for new features), a findings tracking loop (owner, SLA, retest), and a hard "no gate-less merge" rule.
remediation.gold_standard: Five scan categories failing in CI, findings tracked to closure within SLA, DAST regularly scheduled, threat modelling on all new boundaries.

remediation.quick_win: bring migrations under tooling (alembic/flyway/prisma), reconcile the drift between envs with a verified baseline, add a CI "fresh build from migrations" check.
remediation.structural: adopt expand-contract migration practice (expanding then contracting changes, reversible when possible), split long migrations into batched incremental jobs, freeze manual-DDL policy, build from migrations as the only path to a new env.
remediation.gold_standard: Migrations are the only way the schema changes; environments provably identical from clean builds; migrations are reversible and fast; zero manual DDL.

remediation.quick_win: document all cross-service DB reads/writes (the hidden map), move the worst cross-read behind an API or event.
remediation.structural: bounded-context data ownership with a public API/event boundary per service, migrate stored-proc logic into application code, run schema ownership checks in CI.
remediation.gold_standard: Each service owns its tables; cross-context access is via API/events only; zero business logic in stored procedures; a change to one context can't break another.

remediation.quick_win: add the missing FKs/unique indexes (backfill orphans first, then constraint), fix the top data-quality violations.
remediation.structural: constraints-when-shipping policy, data-quality probes as recurring CI/data checks, typed columns everywhere, a data steward owns integrity.
remediation.gold_standard: FKs + constraints close to 100%, integrity probes green, zero known duplicate/orphan patterns, cleanup jobs retired.

remediation.quick_win: stand up a read side (index the files into a modern store, keep legacy as archive), build the extraction utilities.
remediation.structural: a data-migration program — move systems of record to maintained technology one store at a time (strangler pattern for data), keep legacy read-only during migration, archive what's truly dead.
remediation.gold_standard: All systems-of-record on maintained technology; legacy formats readable/exportable or archived with access paths; critical data queryable with modern tooling.

remediation.quick_win: index the exploitable gaps that full-table scans reveal, split the hot row (counter → per-shard), add read replicas for read-heavy load.
remediation.structural: bounded-context data design (DATA-02), remove the contention points (sequence/counter patterns rewritten), tuned isolation levels where safe, load tests with concurrency in CI, capacity per feature, not per "make it bigger."
remediation.gold_standard: Lock waits near zero at peak, index strategy documented and maintained, scaling via standard horizontal levers, load tests show headroom > 3×.

indicators.name: Data Lifecycle Management Deficits
indicators.raw_effort: ⚡ ≤ 30 min to inspect; 🔷 for a real restore drill.

remediation.quick_win: prove restore works this week (schedule a drill), set retention tiers, stop seeding dev with PII.
remediation.structural: automated backup verification, retention/archival jobs, PII minimization (anonymization in non-prod), erasure workflow as software, RTO/RPO SLOs with drills scheduled.
remediation.gold_standard: Restore drills quarterly and green, retention automated, zero PII sprawl in dev, erasure request fully exercisable, RTO/RPO met.

remediation.quick_win: fix the top 10 N+1s with eager loading/joins, add the missing indexes on the hot path, reduce column projection.
remediation.structural: query budget per endpoint (assert queries-per-request in tests), index strategy documented and reviewed, offload heavy reads (search, aggregates) to appropriate engines, performance tests with realistic data volume in CI.
remediation.gold_standard: Query counts per endpoint budgeted and tested, N+1 class eliminated, index strategy current, p95 latency flat as data grows 10×.

remediation.quick_win: kill the obvious versioned/flags columns behind an additive migration, document the domain model properly.
remediation.structural: remodel around domain facts — normalize flags into real entities, adopt effective-dating/event structures for changeable rules (see DATA-09), a domain model owned by the team, schema reviewed as domain design not storage plumbing.
remediation.gold_standard: Schema expresses domain facts; product rule changes land without schema surgery; events/snapshots support evolution; archaeology columns gone.

remediation.quick_win: add an append-only event/audit log for the top 3 core aggregates going forward (capture authoritative mutation events, not screenshots).
remediation.structural: eventing strategy for core facts (outbox, event store, or time-boxed history), as-of query support, replay/drills, compliance-backed retention of the history.
remediation.gold_standard: Core aggregates are fully evented with versioned state; as-of queries are routine and tested; history feeds audit and analytics directly.

remediation.quick_win: run diffs, reconcile to the migration baseline, rebuild staging from migrations.
remediation.structural: migrations-as-only-path for every env, fresh-env CI per PR, schema-diff check in CI (fail on env drift), fixture strategy generated from migrations.
remediation.gold_standard: Zero diffs between baseline and any env; fresh environments reproducible; "prod-only bug" eliminated as a category.

remediation.quick_win: generate accurate specs from code (OpenAPI annotations/`apischema`, `drf-spectacular`, NestJS Swagger), validate specs vs. responses in CI.
remediation.structural: contract-first or contract-enforced development (spec is source of truth, generators produce clients/mocks/tests), a lint gate on spec changes.
remediation.gold_standard: Every endpoint covered by a current, accurate contract; clients and tests generated from it; spec drift impossible (CI enforces).

remediation.quick_win: introduce versioning at the least cost (path `v2` for the contract-breaking surface; keep `v1` alive with a retirement date).
remediation.structural: versioning policy (what counts as breaking), deprecation headers + documented schedule, sunset coach with migration guides, semver discipline wired into release automation.
remediation.gold_standard: Explicit versioning everywhere; breaking changes only in majors with deprecation windows; a deprecation calendar; zero silent consumer breakage for two years.

remediation.quick_win: build the topology map (automated), as the source of truth, and start routing traffic through a gateway for the top 5 hubs.
remediation.structural: platform governance — service registry, gateway/boundary routing, event-based decoupling for the densest paths, rules against direct cross-service DB access.
remediation.gold_standard: Known topology (auto-mapped, current), integration governance (registry/gateway/events), a change to one service locally verifiable, density trending down.

remediation.quick_win: add timeouts + circuit breakers on the fragile hops, cache the slow reads.
remediation.structural: slice the sync chain with events/async (compute off-path, return fast), bulkhead partitions by dependency, SLO-per-hop, degrade gracefully.
remediation.gold_standard: Core flows touch the minimum live dependencies; slow work is async; circuit-broken fallbacks in place; the weakest link cannot sink the product.

remediation.quick_win: wrap the top 3 vendor calls behind ports (adapters), add fallback paths where feasible, assign a vendor-risk owner + deprecation watch.
remediation.structural: integration abstraction for critical vendors, SLA monitoring + circuit breakers, contract/license review, documented replacement paths, vendor deprecation calendar.
remediation.gold_standard: External dependencies abstracted, fallbacked, monitored, and reviewed; vendor deprecations tracked and migrations planned; no revenue path is call-vendor-and-pray.

remediation.quick_win: stand up modern endpoints (REST/JSON or gRPC) alongside the legacy ones for new traffic, put a gateway in front to let consumers choose.
remediation.structural: migrate integrations off legacy protocols where feasible (strangler at the protocol layer), retire the EOL middleware, offer modern contracts for every legacy consumer.
remediation.gold_standard: Core traffic on modern protocols, legacy formats behind adapters/bridges and shrinking, no EOL middleware, new integrations never require the museum stack.

remediation.quick_win: standardize an error contract (RFC 7807 or a JSON schema: code, message, correlationId, retriable flag), add request IDs everywhere, fix the worst misclassifications.
remediation.structural: framework-level error middleware (single source of truth), typed error taxonomy, API-monitoring that segments by error class, error payloads free of PII.
remediation.gold_standard: Every endpoint returns structured, typed, correlated errors; 4xx/5xx semantics correct; a failing request is traceable in seconds; clients can act on errors programmatically.

remediation.quick_win: add per-consumer API keys + endpoint analytics (who, what, how often), start a consumer registry doc.
remediation.structural: full usage telemetry (endpoint + field level), a deprecation communication channel (changelog + consumer mailer + status page), consumer onboarding/registration as standard, usage dashboards for product decisions.
remediation.gold_standard: Every consumer known + registered, endpoint/field usage visible, deprecations announced with migration guides, zero surprise consumer breakage.

remediation.quick_win: add an idempotency key + response-replay on the top money flows, add a unique constraint (order/client_ref) as a backstop.
remediation.structural: idempotency as a platform primitive (framework middleware, key storage, replay store), document retry semantics, idempotency tests in CI for all mutation endpoints.
remediation.gold_standard: All state-changing endpoints idempotent + tested, retry policy documented, duplicate side effects impossible.

remediation.quick_win: add an OpenAPI/buf compatibility check to CI (fail on breaking changes), document the additive-change policy.
remediation.structural: schema registry + versioned schemas (event + API), compat gate enforced, consumer-migration process for breaking changes (deprecate → migrate → remove), telemetry of consumers (API-08).
remediation.gold_standard: Compat gates in CI, schema registry current, breaking changes rare and migration-led, event schemas versioned with consumers tracked.

remediation.quick_win: turn on caching, parallelize shards, drop the slow E2E from the merge path (TEST-04), float the slowest 10 tests once.
remediation.structural: a CI budget (SLO on feedback time), dependency pruning (ECOS-06), test-suite redesign (TEST-03), and monitoring of pipeline trend.
remediation.gold_standard: P95 feedback < 10 min; trend flat/declining; no timeouts; every engineer runs the pipeline before merge by habit.

remediation.quick_win: containerize the stack with a one-command up, ship `.env.example`, write a working setup doc, document the "Golden Path."
remediation.structural: hermetic local env (containers, local deps with `testcontainers`), zero shared-remote requirement, setup scripted and CI-tested (a fresh container proves the guide works), "works on my machine" made unfalsifiable.
remediation.gold_standard: `git clone && make dev` brings up a working local system in < 30 min with no external dependencies; the instruction is CI-verified.

remediation.quick_win: implement fast rollback (repo-state rollback, feature flags, DB-migration backup), add canary/smoke checks to catch the common failure classes, post-release verification automation.
remediation.structural: smaller safer deploys (deploy frequency up = risk down), progressive delivery (canary, blue-green), automated rollback + observability slices, DORA tracked and reviewed monthly.
remediation.gold_standard: CFR < 15% and falling, rollback is automated and boring, deploys are small and frequent, no manual prod intervention.

remediation.quick_win: remove freeze/merge windows, do Friday non-events, add a deploy button per service.
remediation.structural: the classic modernization goal — trunk-based dev + feature flags + small CI/CD steps to get deployment-frequency up and lead time down; each elimination of coordination is a DORA win.
remediation.gold_standard: Deploy on demand (multiple/week/service), lead time < 1 day, releases are boring non-events, no release manager role needed.

indicators.name: Onboarding Lead Time to First Production PR

remediation.quick_win: write a "first PR in a day" path (a safe starter ticket + doc patch + tiny config change), assign onboarding buddy + SLA, grant prod deploy gradually but early.
remediation.structural: fix the underlying debts (setup VEL-02, docs DOCS, deploy VEL-03), curriculum-style onboarding (architecture walkthroughs, ADRs), starter-ticket backlog maintained.
remediation.gold_standard: New engineers ship to prod within their first week, via documented path, with a clear map of the safe-to-change surfaces.

remediation.quick_win: pair-and-document the top exclusive modules (forced bus-factor increase), get a second reviewer on every critical file from here on.
remediation.structural: architecture that doesn't need a walking encyclopedia (simplify, DOCS), quarterly rotation of module owners, an "unlearnable-list" audit (which files can no one explain without the author).
remediation.gold_standard: No module with single-author > 50%; anyone can explain/deploy any critical service within a day; a leaving engineer is a 1-day disruption, not an event.

remediation.quick_win: containerize dev for parity, make config canonical (one source of truth, injected per env), stand up a staging clone of prod config.
remediation.structural: full parity — same containers/versions everywhere, IaC for all envs, config as code, "prod reproduction" as a standard step (spin replica to confirm).
remediation.gold_standard: Any environment can be rebuilt to match prod; prod-only bugs are a thing of the past; config drift is zero-diff against the source of truth.

remediation.quick_win: capture the manual steps as a CI/CD job (artifact → deploy), remove direct prod SSH, add an audit log of every deployment.
remediation.structural: full automated promotion (CI build artifact → envs), IaC-managed infra (PERF-06), deploy from immutable artifacts (never from a checkout on a server), prod access by deploy pipeline only.
remediation.gold_standard: Zero manual steps; deploys are CI pipeline promotions with audit; prod editability removed; an audience of "the pipeline did it" for every release.

remediation.quick_win: enforce branch protection with required reviews on core paths, ban direct pushes, add a PR-size lint (split > 400-LOC PRs), publish review-coverage metrics.
remediation.structural: review as a first-class metric (coverage, size, latency tracked), pairing/small-PR culture, a second reviewer on security-adjacent paths, "no unreviewed merge" as an org rule.
remediation.gold_standard: 100% coverage on core paths, median PR < 400 LOC, reviews substantive (comments, not emoji), zero bypasses, review latency < 1 day.

remediation.quick_win: trunk-based basics — short-lived branches < 3 days, protect main + require green CI, delete the oldest release branch with a manual backport policy.
remediation.structural: move to trunk-based development with feature flags (ties ARCH-10), shrink multi-repo coordination via a platform or monorepo_tools strategy, enforce main-always-green with a CI gate.
remediation.gold_standard: Branches live < 3 days, main is always mergeable and green, merges are small and continuous, no merge windows, one logical change fits in one repo/PR.

remediation.quick_win: define a task runner of record (Makefile/Taskfile), add scaffolding commands for the top 3 boilerplates, enable watch mode.
remediation.structural: invest in DX as product work — fast inner loop, generated code, language-server health, CI parity for local checks.
remediation.gold_standard: Inner loop < 1 min, scaffolding for common work, task runner documented and CI-consistent, AI/IDE tooling first-class.

remediation.quick_win: write the top 5 runbooks (drill them), enable fast rollback (VEL-03), add the observability slices that made diagnosis slow (PERF-01).
remediation.structural: incident-on-call excellence — accurate runbooks, ephemeral-infra-friendly rollback, self-healing where possible, every incident gets a blameless postmortem whose actions you actually fund, MTTR tracked as an SLO.
remediation.gold_standard: MTTR < 30 min majority, runbook-based recovery, rollback automated, no incident class repeats, postmortem actions all shipped.

remediation.quick_win: add structured logging + request IDs everywhere (framework middleware), stand up a metrics endpoint with RED/U; USE basics, emit the top 6 metrics.
remediation.structural: OpenTelemetry adoption (auto-instrumentation), tracing across services, an SLO + error-budget loop, observability as a deployment requirement (no deploy without instrumentation).
remediation.gold_standard: Every service emits metrics/logs/traces standardly, requests are correlated end-to-end, dashboards answer latency/errors/capacity in seconds, and "why is it slow" never requires SSH.

remediation.quick_win: containerize the app (it's usually the smallest step), move VM provisioning to IaC (Terraform/cloud-init), codify the laptop script.
remediation.structural: immutable, containerized, orchestrated deployment (K8s/ECS) with IaC for everything, auto-scaling-ready, snowflakes eliminated by rebuild-from-code.
remediation.gold_standard: Everything containerized + IaC-managed, instances are cattle (rebuildable in minutes), scale is a config change, drift impossible by construction.

remediation.quick_win: profile to find the leak(s), bound the caches (TTL + size limit), fix the top 3 resource leaks, enable heap diagnostics.
remediation.structural: memory discipline as a code review concern, load tests that run > 24h to expose slow leaks, resource limits + monitoring (RSS trend), right-size instances to reality.
remediation.gold_standard: No restart ritual; heap flat over weeks; caches bounded and sized deliberately; utilization reviewed; no OOM under 3–5× load.

remediation.quick_win: statelessness fixes (move session/key state to a distributed store), add read replicas + a cache tier to lift the DB ceiling, shard the hottest table.
remediation.structural: the scalability roadmap — decompose the hot path (bounded contexts, API/events per DATA-02), sharding strategy, and a horizontal-efficiency load-test gate (new instance must add value).
remediation.gold_standard: Adding instances scales throughput linearly past the previous wall; vertical spending is an exception not a norm; load tests prove horizontal efficiency.

remediation.quick_win: set HPA/ASG on the top 5 workloads with sane thresholds, add utilization + headroom dashboards, run the scheduled-campaign checklist.
remediation.structural: autoscaling everywhere + telemetry-driven capacity reviewing (monthly), load-testing against forecast demand, SLO-based scaling decisions.
remediation.gold_standard: Autoscaling covers critical workloads; capacity changes are system-driven by policy; spikes are non-events; waste is continuously right-sized.

remediation.quick_win: adopt Terraform/Pulumi for the top resource types (VPC/DB/compute), add drift detection (initial run finds the gap), codify the "documented console changes" retroactively.
remediation.structural: full IaC coverage with state remote + plan-diffs in CI, admin access least-privilege, rebuild-from-code as a tested path, drift = CI failure.
remediation.gold_standard: Everything in code, changes flow through CI-plan-review, drift is zero or alerted, and rebuilding an env is an afternoon exercise.

remediation.quick_win: define SLOs for the top 3 services (latency p95 + availability), measure them with the metrics you added (PERF-01), add a synthetic check for the money path.
remediation.structural: error budgets + burn alerts, a CI perf gate (load-test baseline run on PRs), latency regression reports in the deploy loop, SLO review as a ritual.
remediation.gold_standard: Every service has an SLO, measured and burned-alerted; CI catches perf regressions; latency baselines are historical and trusted.

remediation.quick_win: lazy-init the greedy startup work, trim the boot-time DI/registrations, enable JVM/cache warmup layers.
remediation.structural: runtime modernization (container-native runtimes, startup budget with a gate, deferred-cost architecture), image size budgets, "cold start < 10s" as an autoscaling prerequisite.
remediation.gold_standard: Cold start < 10–15s, idle footprint proportional to need, autoscaling actually scales because instances become useful fast, zero "startup work" that could be lazy.

remediation.quick_win: tag/attribution, kill the obvious idle/orphaned resources, right-size the top 10 oversized instances, set a budget alert.
remediation.structural: FinOps cadence (monthly rightsizing + utilization review), autoscaling-for-cost (scale-to-zero for dev), cost dashboards per team/service, and a cost/request SLO.
remediation.gold_standard: Spend is attributed, tracked vs. usage, auto-right-sized, budgets alert, and waste < 10% of bill with an explanation for the rest.

remediation.quick_win: write the DR plan (real: recover critical path), define RTO/RPO per tier, take documented cross-region snapshots for the critical DB, run a tabletop then a real drill.
remediation.structural: ring-fence the critical path into multi-AZ → multi-region with tested failover, async replication strategy, automated failover runbooks, drills scheduled quarterly as a non-negotiable ritual.
remediation.gold_standard: Critical path survives a region event within RTO (drilled and proven), RTO/RPO documented, drills are boring quarterly calendar items, recovery is automated not theatrical.

remediation.quick_win: write ADRs for the top 10 load-bearing decisions (interview the oldest engineers, mine git/past docs), establish a template + PR requirement for consequential choices.
remediation.structural: ADR convention in the repo (ADR-NNN, status, decision, context, alternatives considered), decisions now documented at review time, an "explain every load-bearing choice" refactoring task.
remediation.gold_standard: Every consequential decision has an ADR with alternatives; new decisions document as standard practice; teams can revisit a decision on evidence, not memory.

remediation.quick_win: a doc-rot sweep (delete/rewrite the worst 10), add "last verified" dates, a github-issues link on every doc page so inaccuracies are reportable with one click.
remediation.structural: docs-as-code with CI verification (commands in docs execute in a test fixture — DOCS-09), ownership per doc, "docs touched in the same PR as code" rule.
remediation.gold_standard: Docs match code; commands in docs are CI-verified; a doc is as trustworthy as code, and updated with it.

remediation.quick_win: write runbooks for the top 5 incident classes today (postmortem-driven), make them linkable from alert dashboards, add "runme at the first sign" steps.
remediation.structural: runbook-as-product (owned, tested, games rehearsed), alert→runbook binding, postmortem = runbook update, drill the top runbook quarterly.
remediation.gold_standard: Every incident class has a current, tested runbook; on-call executes procedures not improv; incident time is dominated by execution, not discovery.

indicators.name: No Onboarding Guide / Developer Setup Docs

remediation.quick_win: write the golden path (clone → setup → run → test → first PR) and verify every command executes, add CONTRIBUTING.md.
remediation.structural: golden path CI-verified (fresh container proves it — DOCS-09), onboarding checklist wired into the ticket system, "setup docs break" = blame-the-repo not the human.
remediation.gold_standard: A new hire takes < 2 hours to a working local env entirely from docs; the setup guide is CI-tested and always current.

remediation.quick_win: run the departure drill on the top module — write the unrecorded facts as docs/ADRs/runbooks, pair-document with the oral experts.
remediation.structural: "write it down or it doesn't exist" culture (every knowledge answer → doc link), knowledge-review on critical modules, retiring the phrase "ask X" in favor of "read the doc," interview-capture sessions for missionaries.
remediation.gold_standard: 90%+ of functional questions answerable from written sources; no module depends on a person's memory; the departure drill yields a weekend, not a collapse.

remediation.quick_win: kill the top 20 misleading/obsolete comments (fix or delete), resolve/add justification for the oldest TODOs, rename the worst identifiers.
remediation.structural: self-documenting-code standards in review (naming, small functions), "why" comments for invariants, comment lint (TODO age alarm), and a "readability" gate on the module most touched on-call.
remediation.gold_standard: Code reads like prose (names carry intent), comments exist only for true "why", TODO-rot is gone, and a reader can trust line 1 to mean line 1.

remediation.quick_win: publish the OpenAPI/spec with a generated reference (Swagger UI/Redoc), add examples for the top 10 endpoints, write an auth quickstart.
remediation.structural: docs generated from contract in CI (spec is source, docs are output — DOCS-09), consumer guides for the top use cases, updated with each contract change, "docs in same PR" rule.
remediation.gold_standard: Every endpoint has a current, generated reference with examples; a stranger self-serves; docs update with the contract in the same change.

remediation.quick_win: adopt a CHANGELOG process (Keep-a-Changelog, auto-generated from commits/PRs), publish release notes for the top consumers, write migration guides for open breaking changes (backfill).
remediation.structural: semantic-release automation (version + changelog + notes automated), a release-communication channel (port status page + email), "breaking = migration guide in same MR" rule.
remediation.gold_standard: Every release has automated notes; every breaking change has a migration guide published with the change; consumers hear first, break never (silently).

remediation.quick_win: wire docs generation into CI (spec → reference), add links/lint checks for markdown, CI-verify the top setup commands (fresh container).
remediation.structural: full docs-as-code — generate what's generatable, verify what's actionable, staleness gates (docs touch-required on code change), docs failures block merge like code failures.
remediation.gold_standard: Docs build like code, generate from truth, verify their own commands, and fail CI on rot — the knowledge layer is as maintained as the code.

remediation.quick_win: name an owner/champion for the docs, run an offboarding knowledge-capture ritual for the top knowledge holders (scripted walkthroughs into docs/ADRs), capture the last 3 departures' gaps retroactively.
remediation.structural: ownership map (every doc/module has a maintainer), offboarding checklist enforced by HR tools, doc health reviews (growth vs. decay) quarterly, documentation as a funded line item not a PTO activity.
remediation.gold_standard: Every knowledge area has an owner; offboarding reliably captures knowledge; departures are 1-day disruptions; the doc library grows while decaying nothing.

remediation.quick_win: a written migration brief (target framework, timeline, budget), framework-but-the-patterns upgrade where feasible, freeze risky features.
remediation.structural: incremental migration (module-shell pattern, route-by-route strangler), contract with the backend (API-01) kept stable during migration, the client on a support-meeting framework within two quarters.
remediation.gold_standard: Framework is current-to-recent, security-supported, ecosystems integrable; migration is an ordinary roadmap item if ever needed.

remediation.quick_win: code-split the routes, defer non-critical vendors, compress/optimize images, set a bundle budget in CI (regression gate), measure with Lighthouse in CI.
remediation.structural: a performance budget (bytes + core vitals) enforced, RUM for field data, on-demand vs. bundled loading for heavy features, service-worker caching.
remediation.gold_standard: Initial JS < 300 KB, LCP < 2.5s on mobile field-data, code-split by route, budget-enforced in CI, vitals tracked on a dashboard.

remediation.quick_win: run axe, fix the top serious/critical violations (labels, semantics, focus, contrast), add a11y lint to CI.
remediation.structural: a11y standards + automated gate (axe in CI failing new violations), keyboard/contrast reviews, component-library a11y defaults, screen-reader smoke tests on core journeys.
remediation.gold_standard: a11y score ≥ 95, zero critical/serious violations, keyboard + screen-reader flows pass in review, a11y gate enforced in CI.

remediation.quick_win: declare the matrix + enforce browserlist, add a responsive bootstrap for the top user journey, test mobile on the core path.
remediation.structural: responsive-first design standards, device/browser QA in the pipeline, analytics-informed matrix reviews twice a year, cut the obsolete matrix (drop IE11 promises, shed polyfills).
remediation.gold_standard: Declared + enforced current matrix, responsive across breakpoints, browser/device tested in QA, matrix reviewed against real usage.

remediation.quick_win: mark the top 3 god-components, extract their clearest slice with a test, introduce a singular state pattern with actions.
remediation.structural: a deliberately small client architecture (one store, typed, actions-only), component decomposition by responsibility, testable seams with a component test budget, codegen for new screens (VEL-11-style).
remediation.gold_standard: God-components ≤ modern norms, single main state path, components testable in isolation with coverage, "touch one page breaks another" is a historical anecdote.

remediation.quick_win: build a token layer (design tokens → styled primitives), consolidate the top 2 duplicate controls, adopt one primitive set for new work.
remediation.structural: a small living component library (owned, versioned), tokens adopted across screens, "no new hand-rolled primitive" rule, design ↔ engineering parity checks.
remediation.gold_standard: One primitive set, tokens everywhere, new screens composed not styled, visual parity across the app by construction.

remediation.quick_win: adopt an i18n framework + extraction automation, move strings to tokens, ship locale toggling, fix the top market's dates/plurals.
remediation.structural: locale as a first-class runtime concept (RTL, pluralization via ICU, locale-aware formatting/sorting), full-fidelity QA per shipped locale, prune markets served with fake translations until real ones are ready.
remediation.gold_standard: All UI strings extracted, ICU-correct plurals per locale, RTL fully supported, dates/numbers locale-aware, per-locale QA completeness, new code requires tokens (lint-enforced).

remediation.quick_win: add a service worker + shell caching (static shell offline), persist draft state, cut mobile payload for the core path, cache-first for static assets.
remediation.structural: PWA/progressive economics by design (offline-first where core), mobile perf budget (Lighthouse gate), reconnect/resume semantics (idempotent submit ties into API-09), context-tiered asset serving.
remediation.gold_standard: Core flows work offline (or degrade meaningfully well), draft data survives navigation, mobile perf within budget, progressive capability measured and tracked.
